messages:
onprem-customer: Hey team, urgent — private VPC deploy can't pull model shards or send telemetry. Deploy logs show TLS handshake failures and 403s to the model registry. App is timing out on inference calls. Support case #58291.

devin: Sorry you're hitting this. Can you paste the exact error lines from the agent logs and a quick curl repro? Also, which installer version?

onprem-customer: Installer v1.7.2. Excerpt from agent.log: 
```
2026-03-15T08:12:07Z [error] fetch shard https://model-registry.redwood.ai/models/gpt-large/shard-0001 -> TLS handshake failed: remote error: tls: handshake failure (SNI mismatch?)
2026-03-15T08:12:09Z [warn] telemetry upload https://telemetry.prod.redwood.ai/api/v1/ingest -> 403 Forbidden
```
Tried curl from the host: `curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/models/gpt-large/shard-0001 --output -` gives `* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)` then `* 403 Forbidden` with short cert chain printed.

maria: Thanks — two common culprits for onprem: TLS interception (corporate MITM/proxy) causing SNI mismatch, or firewall/proxy blocking specific CDN/OCSP endpoints. Can you run `openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood.ai:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai -showcerts` and paste the Subject CN / SANs? Also `openssl s_client -connect ocsp.intel.cdn.example:80 -status` (replace with actual ocsp host from cert).

onprem-customer: ran s_client, cert SANs are for `*.akamaicdn.net` and `model-registry.redwood.ai` not for our proxy host. But when we run from inside the cluster the peer cert CN is our proxy hostname (corp-tls-proxy.local). So sounds like TLS terminate + reissue. We do have a transparent TLS intercepting proxy.

devin: Yep that's the issue. Our model shards are served from an SNI-sensitive CDN and we rely on OCSP stapling/OCSP responder reachability. TLS reissue breaks cert chain validation and signature-based model auth -> leads to 403s and handshake failures.

infra-eng: Quick checklist for network team: allow SNI passthrough (no TLS terminate) for these hosts OR add TLS passthrough rules for the following hostnames and IP ranges and allow outbound 443/80 to OCSP/CDN/resolver endpoints. Minimal hostlist we require: `model-registry.redwood.ai`, `telemetry.prod.redwood.ai`, `artifacts.redwood.ai`, `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `cdn.redwood.ai`, `ocsp.digicert.com`, `ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org`. Also allow DNS (udp/53) to your resolver and egress to NTP.

maria: Adding ports and protocols: 443 (TLS) outbound required, 80 for OCSP/responder redirects, 853 if using DNS-over-TLS, and 443 for auth/token endpoints. If you cannot disable TLS intercept, you must import the intercept CA into the installer/trust store AND ensure SNI string is preserved (some proxies rewrite SNI which still breaks CDN routing).

onprem-customer: Network team pushed that we can't fully disable intercept, but we can whitelist specific hosts. They asked for exact FQDNs and sample curl checks they can run.

devin: Provide them this quick check sequence to validate passthrough vs intercept: `curl -I -v --resolve model-registry.redwood.ai:443:<public-ip> https://model-registry.redwood.ai/` (force connect to public IP) and `curl -v https://model-registry.redwood.ai/ --cacert /etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt`. If the first succeeds but second shows proxy cert, intercept is present. Also check `openssl s_client -connect <public-ip>:443 -servername model-registry.redwood.ai` and compare cert Subject.

infra-eng: We'll also need outbound allowlist for package installs during provisioning: `pypi.org`, `files.pythonhosted.org`, `artifactory.company-cdn.example` (if you mirror). If customers mirror packages through internal artifactory, ensure our installer can reach the mirror or provide a list of allowed package hostnames.

onprem-customer: Network ran the checks. Confirmed intercept for model-registry and ocsp responders. They can add allowlist entries but say the proxy will still resign certs. What's the recommended approach if we can't stop resigning?

maria: Two options: 1) Import proxy CA into the system/trust store used by the Redwood agent and edge services (makes resigning transparent) AND ensure SNI passthrough to preserve hostname (some resigning proxies still rewrite SNI). 2) Configure a dedicated egress NAT/proxy that allows TLS passthrough for our listed hostnames (preferred for security/ease). If you choose (1), we can provide an automated CA import step for the installer.

devin: Also note: token-based auth to model-registry validates cert chain + issuer during shard download. If resigning is used, token validation will fail unless the CA is trusted locally. We'll attach a minimal allowlist + ocsp endpoints file for your network team.

onprem-customer: Please attach that list here and any small changes to the installer for CA import. We need to get inference back online this afternoon.

support-bot: Case #58291 updated: requested network allowlist + CA import instructions. Agent assigned to devin.

maria: I'm pasting the minimal host list and ports below (copy to network team):
- model-registry.redwood.ai : 443 (TLS)
- telemetry.prod.redwood.ai : 443 (TLS)
- cdn.redwood.ai / *.akamaicdn.net : 443 (TLS)
- pypi.org : 443 (TLS)
- files.pythonhosted.org : 443 (TLS)
- ocsp.digicert.com : 80/443 (OCSP responders may redirect)
- ocsp.int-x3.letsencrypt.org : 80/443
- artifacts.redwood.ai : 443
- tokens.redwood.ai : 443 (auth)

maria: Installer CA import snippet (for network team to run if they must resign):
```
# import proxy CA into system (Debian/Ubuntu example)
sudo cp company-proxy-ca.crt /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/company-proxy-ca.crt
sudo update-ca-certificates
# restart redwood agent after import
sudo systemctl restart redwood-agent
```

onprem-customer: Thanks — forwarding to network now. Will update when they confirm. Really appreciate the quick triage. :pray:

devin: Ping here once they confirm. If they want, we can schedule a short call with infra and your network team to walk through the passthrough rules.

onprem-customer: Will do. Last note: we saw a billing spike in the console due to repeated retries — can you pause usage logging for this customer while we triage?

support-bot: Billing hold requested on case #58291. Operations to review.
